newsitem.title: ITALY: Separatist Bossi makes overture to Italian govt.
newsitem.headline: Separatist Bossi makes overture to Italian govt.

text.p: Separatist leader Umberto Bossi made an overture to the Italian central government on Tuesday when he announced he would hold talks with the head of a parliamentary commission studying constitutional reforms.
Bossi, leader of the Northern League party, told reporters before a television appearance in the lagoon city that he would meet Massimo D'Alema at three p.m. (1300 GMT) on Wednesday.

D'Alema is the leader of the Democratic Party of the Left, the biggest force in the centre-left government, and chairman of a special cross-chamber committee known as the "bicamerale" studying how to revamp the second part of Italy's constitution.
"Tomorrow I will outline a series of things to D'Alema and I'll listen to what he has to say," Bossi said.
But he said he did not hold out much hope of progress.

"I don't think we'll get very much out of the bicamerale, especially federalism, because to achieve federalism, article five of the constitution would have to be changed, that is the first part of the constitution, which the bicamerale can't touch," he said.
Article five says the Italian Republic is "one and indivisible (and) recognises and promotes local autonomies".
Bossi, who won popular support on a federalist ticket, declared a self-styled republic of the north called Padania in Venice last September.

But his switch to outright separatism increasingly cost followers and Bossi was criticised for indirectly encouraging a bizarre stunt last Friday when an armed band of separatists occupied the belltower in Venice's famous St Mark's Square.
Bossi distanced his party from the prank but D'Alema said he should prove he was serious by returning to the parliamentary commission, which has less than two months to complete its work.
Bossi said he was returning to the commission as "the mediator between the government of Padania and the Italian system" but said: "I don't see how an accord can be reached."
